what: FTI Consulting provides expert advice in disputes and crises. Its people give evidence in litigation and arbitration, investigate fraud, advise companies in financial distress, assess economic damages and antitrust questions, handle crisis communications and provide technology for legal discovery.
customers: Law firms and their clients in litigation and arbitration, companies under regulatory investigation, boards dealing with distress or activist investors, and government agencies.
money: Expert testimony, damages analysis, antitrust and financial economics.
Advising distressed companies, creditors and bankruptcy estates.
Fraud investigation, electronic discovery and crisis communications.
moat: Expert testimony and investigative work are bought on individual credibility: a law firm hires a named expert whose evidence will stand in court. FTI has assembled a large number of such people across many specialisms, which lets it staff cases other firms cannot. The restructuring practice also earns more when the economy is poor, offsetting the parts that do not.
risks: Only two analysts are reflected in the $186.50 average target, which is below the current price — an unusual signal that the sell side sees the shares as overvalued.
The shares trade at about 25.3 times earnings and 16.3 times EV/EBITDA, which is full for a people business.
Senior experts can leave and take their case relationships with them, and competitors recruit them aggressively.
A net margin of 7.1% is modest, because compensation consumes most of the revenue.
Revenue growth has slowed, from $3.5B in 2023 to $3.8B in 2025, after a faster period.
opportunities: Revenue has grown every year, from $2.8B in 2021 to $3.8B in 2025, with trailing revenue of $4.0B.
Free cash flow of $353.7M against a $5.5B market value, at about 15.7 times free cash flow.
Litigation, investigation and regulatory activity are driven by legal processes rather than by the economic cycle, which makes demand unusually steady.
Debt of $626.7M against $265.1M of cash is light, and the business requires almost no capital.
The restructuring practice is countercyclical, earning more precisely when other advisory work dries up.
watch: Billable headcount and utilisation. In a consulting business, revenue is people multiplied by how busy they are, and both are reported.
view: FTI Consulting sells expertise in situations where being wrong is expensive: a damages calculation that must survive cross-examination, a fraud investigation a board will act on, a restructuring plan creditors will vote on. That makes demand unusually insensitive to the economy, because litigation and regulatory investigation follow legal processes rather than business confidence. A company being sued does not postpone its defence because the economy is soft.

The internal mix adds a further smoothing effect that is genuinely valuable. The restructuring practice earns more when companies are failing, which is precisely when other professional services work dries up. Combined with litigation work that runs regardless, this gives FTI a revenue base more stable than almost any other consulting firm — and the record shows it, with growth every year from $2.8 billion to $3.8 billion.

The asset, however, is entirely human, and it is worth being blunt about what that means. A law firm does not hire FTI; it hires a specific expert whose name goes on the report and who sits in the witness box. If that person moves to a competitor, the cases follow. This is why compensation consumes most of the revenue and why the net margin is 7.1% rather than something that looks like a software company. The firm is in a permanent negotiation with the people who constitute it.

At 25.3 times earnings and 16.3 times EV/EBITDA, with two analysts averaging a target below the share price, the market is paying a quality multiple for a business whose quality depends on retention. That is not a comfortable combination. I rate the business highly and the price less so: billable headcount and utilisation are the two numbers that describe what is actually happening, and a firm paying up to keep people while utilisation softens is the pattern that would concern me most.
bull: Litigation and regulatory demand stays indifferent to the cycle while the restructuring practice offsets any slowdown, and steady headcount growth compounds revenue.
bear: Senior experts depart with their case relationships, compensation absorbs the growth at a 7% margin, and a 25 times earnings multiple on a people business contracts.
